I think your question really attacks a philosophical question:

  • What are the "cool" parts of realism and what are the boring and tedious ones?

The mechanics have to make the game more fun. Something like rumble to simulate fun vibration is undoubtedly cool. And realistic.

But "no saves / no respawns" , while real, aren't fun; I mean, if I wanted to have the ultimate realistic FPS I could join the army. But there are plenty of reasons I don't want to do that.

Being in the military takes a lot of tough, tedious work and the payoff (eg, "fun") isn't that great because the risk is so high (we're talking about fun & gaming now, not salary & benefits).

So you strip out the boring stuff, and keep the elements that make a good game.

No-reloading, in my opinion is fun in every game because it opens up options for gameplay: you can't just spray down every room and you can't always count on having a gun that's always ready to fire. Neither can your enemy. And that opens up fun tactics.

One alternative is to make a weapon which you can fire at full power for limited time and then it fires at lower power. So you have to choose if you wait it out or do the low power firing, depending on situation.

Personally I think that's going a step too far. As annoying as reloading may be, it allows for periods of "down time" between what would otherwise be incessant and tiresome shooting.

On the other hand, I've been proposing the question:

Why do PvE games like Destiny require you to have limited ammunition for your bread-and-butter weapons such as your primary and secondary? Seeing as there's endless hordes of enemies, why not give you infinite ammo (not bottomless clip/not having to reload)? Having to hunt for more ammunition isn't fun. It's tedious. It breaks up the flow of the game completely - unless you design the game's mechanics and weapons around it (like how Destiny handled its heavy weapons - rocket launchers and such) which only really works in competitive multiplayer. The problem is Destiny only did that with its heavy weapons while not giving your primaries infinite ammo - essentially gimping the system (at least from what I can see anyway).
In Serious Sam, you can design the levels so that you have to move around in battle to collect extra ammunition to keep firing your guns.

Mass Effect 2 and 3.

Mass Effect 1 had it and I thought it worked great. If you timed your shots your weapon didn't overheat and you could put a steady stream of shots down range.

Instead of rebalancing and improving on the system, ME2 and 3 decided to throw it away and added in the standard ammo and clip system. So you still spam bullets, but it's interrupted by reloading and ammo collection.
One of the things I hated the most about mass effect 2 was the reloading mechanics. Mass effect 1 did it right.

This would probably need some balancing for it to succeed, but I think that Planetside 2 should have no reload requirements for the Terran Republic. The issue I found with TR was that while their theme is supposed to be 'more bullets!', it comes at almost every single other disadvantage possible; lower power, lower accuracy, longer reload times and such. Having done way better on foot as NC, it occured to me that TR guns could have one big ammo pool without that being too much of an advantage given the burst damage power of NC guns. In the case that it turns out to be too good, some sort of simple heat-management mechanic should sort it out while maintaining the TR theme.
